summary: This paper proposes heterogeneous quantum architectures (HQA) pairing superconducting and neutral-atom platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computing, introducing two design strategies: MagicAcc offloads magic state factories to fast SC devices ($10–100$ ns gates, 99.9% fidelity) while executing computation on scalable NA arrays ($0.1–1$ µs gates, >6000 qubits), and Memory-Compute Separation utilizes NA qLDPC memory for high-density storage while SC provides fast surface-code processing. End-to-end cost modeling demonstrates that HT-MCSep-MAcc achieves $752 ×$ speedup over NA-only baselines and reduces physical qubit footprint by $10.8 ×$ compared to SC-only systems through principled role assignment based on complementary hardware strengths.
motivation: No single qubit modality simultaneously offers optimal operation speed, connectivity, and scalability for FTQC; breakthroughs in quantum interconnects make cross-platform integration viable, enabling specialization analogous to classical heterogeneous computing.
method: We develop a comprehensive HQ-ISA instruction set and parameterized cost model (Sec. IV) for compute, memory, magic-state factories, and cross-modality transport, then analyze speedup via Amdahl-style formulations (Eq. 4 with drivers $S$, $r_T$, $\rho_{\mathrm{MS}}$, $P_{\mathrm{Trans}}$) and space-time trade-offs to map workload properties to optimal architectures.
result: HT-MCSep-MAcc (NA qLDPC memory + NA GBC compute with SC MSF) achieves $237 ×$ speedup over homogeneous NA-MCSep and $10.8 ×$ space reduction relative to SC-only systems, with speedup saturation at $1 + \rho_{\mathrm{MS}}$ where $\rho_{\mathrm{MS}} \approx 1200$ for magic-state cultivation; transport latency up to $10^{-3}$ s remains tolerable.
